headline: Avoiding Insulation Blunders in Your Garage
articleBody: Insulating your garage can make a huge difference in comfort and energy efficiency, but it's easy to make a few common mistakes that can really diminish the benefits. Here's how to avoid them: First, don't install batts with gaps, compression, or miscuts. When insulation is squished or has gaps, its effective R-value drops significantly, creating cold spots and reducing its ability to keep your garage comfortable. Make sure it's snug, but not compressed. Second, ignoring air sealing around penetrations and at rim joists is a big no-no. Many people focus only on the cavity insulation and forget that drafts can sneak in through unsealed gaps, leading to significant energy loss and discomfort. Third, be careful with vapor barrier placement. Using the wrong type of vapor barrier or placing it incorrectly in garages that will be conditioned later can actually trap moisture, leading to mold or material damage over time. It's a tricky balance that depends on your climate. Fourth, never insulate before you've tackled any water intrusion or slab moisture issues. Wet insulation is ineffective insulation and can quickly deteriorate. Address those problems first! Lastly, don't use insulation that doesn't meet the required R-value for garage conversions or skip insulation in critical areas like ceilings above conditioned spaces. This can lead to inspection failures and a less efficient space.
